review_candidates.description: Who we are: In 2014, PLC Group began with a simple but powerful belief: critical facilities deserve more than fragmented systems and delayed insight. They deserve clarity—real-time, reliable, and actionable. Built by experts in Telecom, Data Centres, and Critical Facilities Management, PLC Group grew from firsthand experience. We saw the pressure operators face when visibility is limited, when connectivity fails, and when optimization is more guesswork than science. So we set out to change that. Our mission evolved into a bold vision: to become the world’s leading unification platform for Critical Facilities—empowering organizations everywhere with true Actionable Intelligence. Today, that vision is taking shape across the globe. Tier-1 telecom operators in North America, Europe, and Asia rely on our technologies to keep their critical infrastructure running at peak performance. In Canada, we serve as the exclusive value-added reseller for AIRSYS cooling solutions, further strengthening our ability to deliver end-to-end reliability. With more than 10,000 deployments of our Remote Monitoring & Control (RMC) solution worldwide, we’ve come to deeply understand the challenges our customers face—whether operating in highly developed urban networks or remote, resource-strained environments. And every one of those deployments sharpens the insight that drives our innovation. PLC Group was built for the world’s most demanding environments. And we continue to grow with a single purpose: transforming complexity into clarity and turning data into action. About the Role We are seeking a detail-oriented Systems Integration Technician with hands-on experience in electrical, electronic, and entry-level networking tasks. In this role, you will bridge the gap between hardware assembly, basic system configuration, and functional testing. Whether you are a fresh graduate with strong practical project experience or an early-career technician looking to grow your skills, this role offers direct exposure to control systems, harness preparation, and system-level troubleshooting. Key Responsibilities Electrical & Hardware Assembly: Prepare, assemble, and route cable harnesses; perform electrical wiring and connections based on technical schematics. Testing & Diagnostics: Conduct continuity testing, measure voltage and current using multimeters, and perform end-to-end I/O verification. Network & Controller Setup: Execute basic programming, configure local controllers, and run network diagnostics (ping and latency tests) to ensure stable communication. Schematic Interpretation: Read, analyze, and work directly from basic electrical wiring diagrams and system schematics. Troubleshooting: Identify, isolate, and resolve basic electrical, electronic, and connection faults during assembly and testing phases. Qualifications & Requirements Education: Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Experience: Fresh graduates with strong hands-on project work are encouraged to apply. Core Technical Skills: Fundamental understanding of electrical/electronic principles. Familiarity with multimeters and basic diagnostic tools. Basic knowledge of networking concepts (IP connectivity, latency, ping testing). Familiarity with basic controller or microcontroller configuration. Mindset: Strong practical problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a proactive willingness to learn new technologies.
